principles.statement: Any code path that resets per-request progress state (e.g., ProgressIndex=0 on preemption) must also reverse all cumulative metrics that were incremented based on that progress. Failing to do so causes irreversible metric inflation proportional to the number of preemptions.
principles.regime: Single-instance simulator with KV cache pressure causing preemptions. Validated at 47-348 preemptions across 5 seeds and 3 cache-pressure levels (600, 6000, 60000 blocks).
principles.mechanism: sim/simulator.go:executeBatchStep() increments TotalOutputTokens++ per decode step. sim/batch_formation.go:preemptForTokens() resets ProgressIndex=0 on preemption. Without the fix, tokens counted before preemption are counted again after rescheduling. The fix computes outputTokensLost = max(0, ProgressIndex - len(InputTokens)) before reset and subtracts it in scheduleBatch.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to any simulator metric incremented inside the decode loop before a state reset. Does not apply to cluster-level metric merging paths (untested). ITL slice entries face the same hazard (RP-2).

principles.statement: Per-request slice metrics (e.g., ITL inter-token latency entries) must be cleared on preemption to prevent duplicate entries from accumulating across re-executions of the same decode tokens.
principles.regime: Single-instance simulator with preemptions. Fix validated across 5 seeds and 3 cache-pressure levels. ITL correctness confirmed indirectly: no duplicate ITL entries in output (itl_mean_ms values are in expected range).
principles.mechanism: sim/batch_formation.go:preemptForTokens() appends to result.Preempted. Without ITL clearing, re-execution of the same tokens appends duplicate ITL entries to the same request's ITL slice. The fix: preemptedRequest.ITL = preemptedRequest.ITL[:0] immediately after ProgressIndex reset.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to any per-request append-only slice that accumulates entries during decode. ITL is the only such slice identified. Token-scalar metrics (TotalOutputTokens) fall under RP-1.

principles.statement: The preemption output-token double-counting fix (OutputTokensLost subtraction) is robust across seed variation (5 seeds tested) and across preemption regimes (47 preemptions in unit test, 47-72 moderate, 265-348 high). The fix produces exact token-count equality in all tested conditions.
principles.regime: qwen/qwen3-14b model, rate=20 req/s, num_requests=200, seeds [42, 123, 456, 789, 1337], total_kv_blocks in {600, 6000, 60000}. Iter-2 full experiment.
principles.mechanism: The OutputTokensLost computation is algebraically correct: it captures exactly the decode tokens that were counted but will be re-generated. max(0, ProgressIndex - len(InputTokens)) = 0 for prefill-stage preemptions, positive for decode-stage preemptions. The subtraction is exact (integer arithmetic, no rounding). Seed variation confirms no edge-case code path exists that bypasses the fix.
principles.applicability_bounds: Validated for single-instance runs without cluster routing. Cluster-level metric merging (sim/cluster/cluster.go) is not covered. The fix is in sim/ (library layer) and applies to both blis run and blis replay paths.
